header.title: Welcome to pmMDA - poor man's Model Driven Architecture -

section.title: Introduction
section.p: The pmMDA – poor man MDA - tool is a pragmatic approach to use MDA approach in commercial and industrial projects. Tedious source artifacts are generated from a model instead of being hand coded. Talented developers should concentrate on application design and not on writing repetitive code. Currently pmMDA provides extensive support for Java client/server applications using JDBC – meaning 2 tiers programs -, CORBA and J2EE middleware are supported. Work is under way to support C++ based applications.

pmMDA reads UML models, e.g. from ArgoUML tool, extends them with tagged values and generates the source code and configuration artifacts for the target applications. The tagged values are described in the user manual and are legal extensions to the UML method. Therefore the models can still be edited with UML tools. The pmMDA provides a user interface simplifying the edition and validation of tagged values.

The MDA approach becomes powerful when available frameworks provides powerful abstraction to progam against. The pmMDA project provides a set of complete frameworks streamlining client server program development.

section.title: Resources
section.p: The pmMDA provides the following sets of resources.
pmMDA engine defining the metamodel to describe your application and the execution engine executing the cartridges. The model can be defined in a UML such ArgoUML and imported in pmMDA.
A set of cartridges generating the source code and configuration artifacts to run the application. The cartridges are written in Java. The generation template uses the Jakarta Velocity project.

Frameworks simplifying the development of complex mission-critical applications. One of the provided framework implements a data object graph manipulation framework and persistence. We are looking at JSR-235 to standardize this approach. The persistence is realized using the Apache OJB project. A second framework provides a explorer framework to visualize and manipulate graphs of objects using the tree list paradigm.

section.title: Documentation
section.p: Each subproject has its own set of documentation and tutorials. The public interfaces and methods are described in the API documentation generated with JavaDoc.
A seperate section of the site provides articles and presentations about design and implementation aspects of the subprojects.

section.title: Quality and Metrics
section.p: Quality metrics are provided for all hosted projects. The pmMDA Group adheres to the agile process philosophy. Release often, do not wait until it is perfect. But in the long term the quality of the source code and documentation should pass all defined quality criteria. The group provides metrics for all source code and documentation artifacts of the project.
